case_text:
An 85-year-old man with hypertension and paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, not on Coumadin after a prior INR of 18, presented with severe dry mouth after starting a BPH medication. In the ED, he developed AF with RVR to the 130–140s and received multiple IV/PO diltiazem doses with partial improvement. He had mild AKI and received 2 L normal saline. On the floor, his heart rate remained difficult to control with IV/PO nodal-blocking agents, and he developed worsening hypoxia, wheezing, and confusion. IV furosemide 40 mg ×2 produced minimal response, prompting transfer to the CCU for persistent AF with RVR and worsening CHF.

Home medications: Metoprolol tartrate, aspirin, diltiazem, furosemide.
Vitals: ED initial T 98, HR 68, BP 148/113, RR 16, O2 sat 96% RA, FSBS 142; floor T 98.1, HR 120–140 → 100–120 after IV/PO rate control, BP 138/96, RR 18, O2 sat 98% RA.
Labs: BNP 24117 | trop 0.02 | Cr 1.9 | K 5.6 | BUN 39 | Na 143.

Physical exam: NAD, lying in bed; dry mouth; lungs CTAB; irregularly irregular, tachycardic, systolic murmur at apex; abdomen soft, NT/ND; no edema; A+Ox3.

Echo: LVEF 30% with moderately depressed LV systolic function and moderate symmetric LV hypertrophy; mildly dilated RV with borderline normal free-wall function, septal motion consistent with RV pressure overload; moderate to severe aortic stenosis, valve area 0.9 cm²; moderate to severe mitral and tricuspid regurgitation; moderate pulmonary artery systolic hypertension; small to moderate circumferential pericardial effusion without tamponade. Compared with prior, LV function newly impaired and AS/MR/TR increased.

ECG: AF with rapid ventricular rate; nonspecific diffuse ST abnormalities, likely rate-related; rate 141, QRS 90, QT/QTc 326/467; possible atrial flutter, PVCs or aberrant conduction, LVH.

CXR: moderate cardiomegaly and central pulmonary vascular engorgement consistent with fluid overload; small bilateral effusions with probable left lower-lobe collapse/consolidation.
Renal ultrasound: simple bilateral renal cysts; no hydronephrosis.
RUQ ultrasound: gallbladder wall thickening without stones, distention, or pericholecystic fluid, possibly third spacing; right pleural effusion.
Procedures: arterial line placement.

system_a.dx: DIAGNOSIS: Acute on chronic systolic HF; HFrEF, LVEF 30%.
system_a.causes:
CONTRIBUTORS: AF with rapid ventricular response; aortic stenosis; mitral and tricuspid regurgitation; secondary pulmonary hypertension.
COMPLICATIONS: Acute kidney injury, hyperkalemia, congestive hepatopathy.
COMORBIDITY: Hypertension.
system_a.acute:
UP-TITRATE: Furosemide.
CONTINUE: Metoprolol tartrate — acute AF rate control.
START: Sodium zirconium cyclosilicate — for 48 hours, then reassess potassium.
system_a.gdmt:
START: Metoprolol succinate.
START: Dapagliflozin.
START: Sacubitril-valsartan.
START: Spironolactone.
START: Amiodarone — initial and maintenance regimens.
START: Apixaban.
STOP: Diltiazem, fludrocortisone, aspirin.
STOP: Digoxin, potassium chloride, tolterodine — specified in safety actions.
CONTINUE: Omeprazole, citalopram; lactulose as needed.
system_a.monitor:
MONITOR: ECG every 3 days — QTc risk with amiodarone, citalopram, and haloperidol.
MONITOR: Renal function every 3 days during therapy initiation.
LIMIT: Citalopram dose in elderly patients.
TRANSITION: Heparin to apixaban — at least 6-hour interval stated in output; source instruction is truncated.
SAFETY RATIONALE: Digoxin-amiodarone interaction and renal impairment; potassium supplementation with hyperkalemia; tolterodine anticholinergic risk; diltiazem negative inotropy in HFrEF.
REQUEST: Dobutamine stress echocardiogram; technetium-99m PYP scan for ATTR amyloidosis; serum/urine protein electrophoresis with free light chains.
system_a.dispo:
FOLLOW-UP: Outpatient echocardiogram in 3–6 months after rate control and GDMT optimization.
LEVEL OF CARE / DISCHARGE CRITERIA: Not documented in the supplied output.

system_b.dx: Acute decompensated heart failure with newly reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF, LVEF 30%). Hemodynamic profile warm and wet.
system_b.causes: Precipitants: AF with RVR, 2 L normal saline, IV diltiazem in the setting of reduced EF. Structural: AS, MR/TR, pulmonary hypertension. Complications: AKI, hyperkalemia, delirium. Comorbidities: hypertension. Other: anticholinergic effect of the BPH medication; possible LLL pneumonia.
system_b.acute: Furosemide 80 mg IV BID with goal net negative 1–2 L/day. Stop diltiazem; start IV amiodarone for rate control. Stop potassium supplements; sodium zirconium cyclosilicate and recheck K in 6 hours. Stop IV fluids; fluid restriction 1.5 L/day.
system_b.gdmt: Amiodarone; start metoprolol succinate once euvolemic; stop diltiazem. Hold ARNI/ACEi/ARB until Cr and K improve. Hold MRA while K is high. Start dapagliflozin once renal function is stable. Heparin, then apixaban 2.5 mg BID; stop aspirin. Stop KCl. Stop the BPH anticholinergic.
system_b.monitor: Telemetry; daily ECG for QTc. BMP and Mg BID; TSH and LFTs. Daily weights and strict I/O. PYP scan; structural heart consult. Avoid other QT-prolonging drugs. TEE before any cardioversion.
system_b.dispo: CCU until rate controlled and off IV diuretics and oxygen. Discharge when euvolemic, HR < 110, stable Cr and K. HF clinic within 7 days; structural heart evaluation.
